To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inter-ictal interval is the most important determinant of ictal frequency in man.

the spontaneous epileptiform activity of man, when recorded by radio telemetry, is characterized by a diurnal rhythm and a quasi-normal distribution of ictal events and inter-ictal intervals, and that nocturnal spike activity is interrupted by REM sleep.

(1) The duration of seizure and inter-seizural intervals are related in man; (2) The distribution of ictal events during day and night is different; (3) Spikes occur with a relatively constant rate during the day and night; (4) Spike occurrence is related to sleep stages; (5) The occurrence of clinical seizures is related to sleep stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the temporal relationships between spontaneous seizures and the normal circadian and ultradian rhythms of the human electroencephalogram (EEG).
the study of the ultradian rhythms of spontaneous seizure dis- charges in man.
the ultradian periodicities of human epileptic seizures.

ultradian rhythms are a characteristic feature of spontaneous seizure activity, and may provide a useful tool for the study of seizure mechanisms and for the design of anticonvulsant drug therapy.
the ictal and inter-ictal phenomena in man are not random but are subject to a variety of ultradian influences.
the ictal and inter-ictal events of human epilepsies are not randomly distributed, but rather follow an ultradian rhythm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultradian rhythms in the human EEG, which we have described in detail, may be related in part to the ultradian rhythms of REM sleep.
the ultradian periodicity of spontaneous epileptiform activity is a manifestation of an intrinsic ultradian periodicity in the human brain.
the spontaneous seizure discharge is a complex, highly regulated phenomenon, which is subject to ultradian periodicity.

the ultradian rhythms of spontaneous seizure discharge in humans, as in animals, may be related to the sleep-waking cycle.
